citation.title: AI Evals For Engineers & PMs
citation.year: 2026 (cohort Sep 5 - Oct 3, 2026; material refined over a year of prior cohorts)

claims.planned: The course exists, taught by Shankar & Husain
claims.finding: Course 'AI Evals For Engineers & PMs' is live on Maven, taught by Hamel Husain ('ML Engineer with 25 years of experience', previously Airbnb and GitHub) and Shreya Shankar ('ML Systems & Applied AI Evals Researcher', PhD from UC Berkeley, joining Carnegie Mellon as Assistant Professor in 2027). Current cohort: Sep 5 - Oct 3, 2026; $4,200; 17 live sessions over 4 weeks.
claims.quote: AI Evals For Engineers & PMs ... Hamel Husain - ML Engineer with 25 years of experience ... Shreya Shankar - ML Systems & Applied AI Evals Researcher
claims.location: Course landing page header / instructor bios

claims.planned: Confirm current curriculum themes: instrumenting agents, error analysis, designing judges aligned with expert judgment
claims.finding: All three themes appear verbatim as course outcomes: agent instrumentation with inspectable traces, a repeatable error-analysis process replacing spot-checking, and LLM-as-judge/code-based evals validated against expert judgment. Syllabus lessons include 'L1: Building Agents, Foundations', 'L2: Building Agents, Designing for Evaluability', 'L3: Error Analysis, Finding Failures'. Additional themes: CI/CD regression testing, red-teaming for safety, cost/accuracy optimization.
claims.quote: Instrument a real agent so every run leaves a trace you can inspect. ... Replace random spot-checking with a repeatable way to read traces and spot failures. ... Design and validate LLM-as-judge and code-based evals that match expert judgment.

claims.planned: Confirm scale claim (~700+ or more engineers/PMs taught)
claims.finding: The current page claims 4,500+ engineers and PMs, not ~700+. The '700+' figure is stale; the course also shows a 4.7 rating from 879 reviews. If citing scale, use '4,500+ engineers and PMs from teams like OpenAI, Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft' (as of June 2026).
claims.quote: refined this exact material over a year of cohorts with 4,500+ engineers and PMs from teams like OpenAI, Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft
claims.location: Course landing page, instructor credibility section

teachable_points.point: Error analysis should be a repeatable process of reading traces, not ad-hoc spot-checking
teachable_points.quote: Replace random spot-checking with a repeatable way to read traces and spot failures.

teachable_points.point: Agents must be designed for evaluability from the start: instrument so every run produces an inspectable trace
teachable_points.quote: Instrument a real agent so every run leaves a trace you can inspect. ... L2: Building Agents, Designing for Evaluability

teachable_points.point: Judges (LLM-as-judge or code-based) are only trustworthy when validated against expert judgment
teachable_points.quote: Design and validate LLM-as-judge and code-based evals that match expert judgment.

teachable_points.point: Evals belong in CI/CD as regression tests, plus red-teaming for safety and cost/accuracy optimization as downstream curriculum themes
teachable_points.quote: CI/CD integration for regression testing; Red-teaming for safety; Cost and accuracy optimization (curriculum themes)

teachable_points.point: The course frames its target audience around an evals anti-pattern: shipping prompt changes without measurement
teachable_points.quote: Engineers and PMs who ship prompt changes and hope nothing breaks.

teachable_points.point: Field-tested at large scale across major AI labs and big tech
teachable_points.quote: refined this exact material over a year of cohorts with 4,500+ engineers and PMs from teams like OpenAI, Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft
teachable_points.numbers: 4,500+ students; rating 4.7 (879 reviews); $4,200; 17 live sessions; 4 weeks; 3-5 hrs/week

misconceptions_to_avoid: Do NOT cite '~700+ engineers/PMs taught' — the current page says 4,500+ (the 700 figure is from an earlier snapshot of the course).
Do not describe it as a generic 'prompt engineering' course — the curriculum is structured around building/instrumenting agents, error analysis, and judge validation.
The course is by both instructors jointly under Parlance Labs on Maven; do not attribute it to only one of them.
notes_for_authors: Strong core source. The three pillars (instrument agents for traces, repeatable error analysis, judges validated against expert judgment) are quoted verbatim on the live page and map cleanly onto a measurement-validity narrative. Update any scale claim to '4,500+ engineers and PMs' (verified 2026-06-09); the page is a live marketing page so numbers (rating 4.7/879, price $4,200, cohort dates Sep 5 - Oct 3 2026) will drift — date-stamp them. Syllabus lesson titles available: L1 Building Agents Foundations; L2 Building Agents, Designing for Evaluability; L3 Error Analysis, Finding Failures (14 more sessions not enumerated on page).
